(Exparte)
 JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That, on 24.12.2022 at about 8.50 to 8.55 a.m. the petitioner was pedestrian in front of BHEL bus stop, outer ring road, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru City, at that time rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-16-EU- 0017 rode the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

3. It is further stated that, immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Shreyas Hospital, Bengaluru wherein she was treated as an outpatient and had spent Rs.50,000/- towards medicines, attendant charges, food and nourishment etc.
4.

It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale, healthy and aged about 33 years, doing coolie and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month and she used to spend the said amount for the maintenance of her family members.
After the accident, she could not do any work due to her severe injuries.
5. It is contended that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-16-EU-0017.

In this regard, case was registered against rider of said vehicle by the jurisdictional Rajajinagara Traffic Police in Crime No.283/2022 under section 279,
337 and 338 of IPC.
As such, the respondent No.1 being the RC insurance company and the respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition seeking compensation.
6. After registration of the case, notices were issued to the respondents.

In response to the notices,
the Respondent No.1/Insurance company has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.

On the other hand, respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court, remained absent,

sentences.text: 7. Brief averments of the Written statement of the Respondent No.1 are as follows:

In the written statement, the respondent No.1 admitted about the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motor cycle bearing No.KA-16-EU-0017 and its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It is contention of the respondent No.1 that alleged accident occurred due to the negligence of the Petitioner.
Further contended that the rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the petition.
Ultimately stated that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner, is highly excessive, exorbitant and without any basis.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 24.12.2022 at about 8.50 to 8.55 a.m. infront of BHEL bus stop, outer ring road, Nandini Layout due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-16-EU-0017 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

from whom?
3) What order or award?
9. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner, petitioner has placed her affidavit evidence in lieu of examination-in-chief, who examined as PW1 and got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has not adduced any rebuttal evidence in order to disprove the contention of the petitioner.

10. Heard the arguments of both the counsel and perused the materials available on record.
11.

My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3:

As per final order,

sentences.text: It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 16/EU-0017, the alleged accident had taken place, consequently she had sustained grievous injuries.

13. On the other hand, the respondent No.1 being the insurance company, though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, seriously disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-16-EU-0017.
The respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle placed exparte.
In the light of the rival contentions of both the parties, on going through the above issue burden is on the petitioner to prove the above issue on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
14. The petitioner in order to prove her case examined herself as PW1.
She has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of her oral evidence has relied upon Ex.
P1 to P7.
Ex. P1-true copy of the F.I.R. Ex.P2-true copy of the first information statement given by one Mahesh, Ex.P3-true copy of the mahazar.
Ex. P4-spot sketch, Ex
.P5-true copy of the IMV report,
Ex.P6-true copy of the wound certificate, Ex.P7-true copy of the charge sheet in Crime No.283/2022 of Rajajinagara Traffic Police Station.

15. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that based upon the first information statement given by one Mahesh, the S.H.O. of Rajajinagara Traffic Police has registered the case against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337 and 338 of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the Investigation Officer of the case has filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.
16.
The respondent No.1 is not chosen to lead its side evidence.

17. The PW1 was subjected to cross-examination at length, but nothing has been elicited from the mouth of the PW1 that this accident is not due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.

18. After careful scrutiny of Police documents i.e., FIR, Complaint, Spot Mahazar, Spot sketch, IMV report, Wound Certoficate and Charge sheet and in the light of the evidence placed by Petitioner, I am of the view that, the Petitioner has placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-16/EU-0017 and in the said accident, the Petitioner sustained injuries.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by her in the accident under different heads.

20. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the Petitioner about the injuries sustained by her,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.

"
21. Pain and Sufferings; PW1 has stated in her evidence that, she has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries she has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P6.

The said document discloses that, she had sustained the following injuries:-
1) Lacerated wound over right temporal region 2) Open deep lacerated wound over left middle shaft of tibia anterior aspect 7x3x4 cms 3) Small insized wound over lateral aspect of right pelvis
The doctor is of the opinion that the injury No.1 & 2 are grievous in nature and the injury No.3 is simple in nature.
By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and opinion of the doctor, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.60,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

22. Loss of income during treatment period:
PW1 has stated that, she was doing coolie and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
In this regard, she has not placed any iota of documents to show the income of the petitioner.
In such a situation, as per law, notional income has to be taken.
It is relevant to note herein that, the petitioner has taken treatment as an outpatient.

By taking into consideration of the said aspect, I am of the view that, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/-
towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.
23. Medical Expeneses;
The petitioner in connection with her treatment expenses, at the time of her evidence, placed medical bills of Rs.6,000/- as per Ex.P10.
At the time of cross- examination suggested that, the medical bills are created for the purpose of her case.
But the respondent No.1 has not palced any dcouments to show that the medical bills produced by the petitioner is created for the purpose of this case.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.6,000/- towards medical expenses.

24. Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges:
The petitioner herein has stated that due to the accidental injuries she had spent huge amount towards conveyance, food & nourishment etc.
The Petitioner has produced OPD slip issued by Shreyas hospital as per Ex.P9, but not produced discharge summary.
As per the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained grievous and simple injuries and has taken treatment as an outpatient.
The petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.
25. Loss of future income;
The petitioner herein is asserting that, she had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by her.

Except the production of wound certificate and OPD slip and averments made in the main petition as well as in the chief affidavit, has not made an effort to examine the treated doctor and not produced any estimation for her future medication in order to prove the disability sustained by her, due to the accidental injuries in order to know, whether the injuries sustained by the petitioner will effect to her future and whether the said injuries will make any discomfort to the petitioner to do her routine work as well as her work for her avocation.
In such a situation, court cannot consider the loss of future income, in the absence of convincing evidence from the side of the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for the compensation under the head of loss of future income and also under the head future medication, due to want of evidence on record.

26. Loss of amenities;
. PW1 has stated in her evidence that due to the accidental injuries she could not do any work.

On going through the injuries mentioned in the wound certificate submitted by the petitioner herein and also in the light of the entire facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that, the Sumangala vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18404542/

29. IABILITY:
As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the Motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-16/EU-0017 alleged accident had taken place.
As already it is discussed in the issue No.1 that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-16/EU-0017.
As such, the respondent No.1 being the insurance company and the respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.1, being the insurance company and indemnifier has to satisfy the award.

In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a.
from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
